devices.title: Add devices
devices.intro: Each function of your heat pump gets its own device in Homey. Ticked devices have live data.
devices.select_one: Select at least one device to add.
devices.main_desc: Overview: outdoor temperature, operating priority and mode, plus diagnostics and statistics
devices.analytics_desc: Helps the developer see which models and features are used and where setup fails. No personal data, readings or network details are sent. You can change this later in the app settings.

sources.prompt: More than one sensor can report this. Choose the one to use:

tank.title: Hot water tank
tank.hint: Required for the hot water estimate. Choose your tank's series, such as VPB. The lining doesn't matter.
tank.inlet_hint: 10 °C is the usual figure; a little lower in winter, higher in summer.

setup.title: Device setup
setup.intro: Set up the functions you selected.
setup.heating_intro: Smart mode, indoor temperature and thermostat zone.
setup.nibe: Use your heat pump’s own temperature sensor
setup.homey: Use your own Homey temperature sensors
setup.promise: Let your rooms guide the heating
setup.promise_desc: Use the temperature sensors you already have in Homey. Choose one room, or average several for a temperature that represents your home. Your heat pump keeps its thermostat and Smart Price Adaption.
setup.picker_intro: Find sensors by name, room, device type or app. Choose one or combine several.
setup.review_intro: Each selected sensor has equal influence.
setup.pending_hint: Add your devices first, then finish the setup in Heating → Repair. Until then, keep your NIBE sensor in control. No temperatures are sent during pairing.
setup.pump_intro: Check these settings on your heat pump, then verify here.
setup.pump_enable: Let your heat pump take a room temperature from Homey. Turn on external room sensor BT50 in menu 7.5.9.2.
setup.pump_zone: Assign BT50 to your heating zone in Room sensor settings and Zones (menu 1.3.3 and 1.3.4).
setup.pump_control: Tell your heat pump to heat by BT50. Remove the sensor it used before if you're replacing it.
setup.zone_confirm: BT50 is set to control the right zone.
setup.verified: Your heat pump received the temperature at BT50.
setup.active_note: Temperature updates keep running in the background. To stop them, return to your NIBE sensor in Heating setup.
setup.handover_hint: On your heat pump, set your original sensor to control the zone and turn off external BT50. Temperature updates continue until you verify here.
setup.handover_confirm: My NIBE sensor is controlling the zone again.
setup.no_nibe_sources: No other sensors found on your heat pump. The current one is kept.
setup.thermostat_zone_title: Which zone should the thermostat set?
setup.thermostat_zone_intro: Your heat pump has more than one zone. Choose the one that controls the heating. On your heat pump, it's the zone whose room sensor is set to control (menu 1.3.3).
setup.analytics_benefit: Nibe Live is built by one developer with one heat pump. Sharing how the app works with yours helps uncover compatibility issues, improve setup and focus development on the features you use.
setup.analytics_details: Includes your heat pump model, app features used and technical events such as setup failures and connection problems. Temperature readings, device names and Flow names are never included.
setup.analytics_optional: Optional. Turn it off anytime in device settings → Privacy.
setup.source_intro: Choose which sensor your heating uses for the indoor temperature.
setup.source_homey_desc: One sensor, or the average of several rooms.
setup.feed_short: Verifying starts temperature updates. They continue after you close Repair.
setup.feed_recovery: If Homey or a sensor stops reporting, BT50 can raise an alarm. Switch back to your NIBE sensor and turn off external BT50 on your heat pump.
setup.zone_detail: Menus 1.3.3 / 1.3.4 · Assign BT50 to the zone you want to heat.
setup.control_detail: Replace the previous controlling sensor if needed.
setup.success_description: Your heat pump is now receiving temperatures from your Homey sensors.

smart.title: Smart mode
smart.section_heating: Who moves heating to cheaper hours.
smart.section_hotwater: Who moves hot water to cheaper hours.
smart.intro: Pick one. Only one planner can run at a time.
smart.choose_on_desc_heating: Learns your house, then heats a little more before expensive hours and a little less during them.
smart.choose_on_desc_hotwater: Learns when your household uses hot water, then heats it in the cheapest hours.
smart.choose_spa_desc: Built into your heat pump. Gets prices through myUplink.
smart.choose_off_desc_hotwater: Hot water follows your heat pump's own settings.
smart.success_description: Status is on the Heating device, Away on Main. The thermostat sets the comfort temperature, and Heating setup sets the comfort range.
smart.spa_note: Autopilot turns off Smart Price Adaption for heating.
smart.indoor_missing: Set up the indoor temperature under Heating first.
smart.outdoor_forecast: Weather forecast. A sensor in the shade is more accurate.
smart.prices_fixed: Fixed price, so nothing to shift. Set dynamic prices in Homey Energy.
smart.room_control_on: This is on in your heat pump. Turn it off to enable Autopilot.
smart.room_control_unknown: Couldn't be read. Keep it off.
smart.bt1: Let Autopilot send the outdoor temperature (BT1)
smart.bt1_detail: On your heat pump, menu 7.5.9.2. Turn on external BT1.
smart.verify_intro: Autopilot checks that your heat pump takes its outdoor temperature.
smart.return_reminder: On your heat pump, turn off external BT1 in menu 7.5.9.2.
smart.outdoor_intro: Pick a sensor in the shade, or use the forecast.
smart.steer_intro: Pick one. Only one planner can run at a time.
smart.pump_intro: What your heat pump needs for your choices.
smart.room_control_optional: Optional. When on, your heat pump adjusts heating by room temperature. Must be off for Autopilot.
smart.pump_confirm: These are set on your heat pump
smart.row_cheaper: Heats more when power is cheap, less when it's expensive
smart.row_learns: Learns how your house holds heat
smart.cmp_note: Smart Price Adaption is built into your heat pump and gets prices through myUplink.
smart.ctl_range_sub: How far the indoor temperature may vary
smart.ctl_away_sub: A lower temperature while you're on holiday
smart.ctl_off_sub: Your heat pump takes over again
smart.section_pool: Who moves pool heating to cheaper hours.
smart.section_cooling: Who moves cooling to cheaper hours.
smart.choose_on_desc_pool: Will heat the pool in cheap and solar hours, within a band you set.
smart.choose_on_desc_cooling: Will pre-cool before price peaks and on solar surplus.
smart.choose_off_desc_pool: The pool follows your heat pump's own settings.
smart.choose_off_desc_cooling: Cooling follows your heat pump's own settings.
smart.hw_intro: A few things before Autopilot takes over hot water.
smart.hw_tank_intro: Autopilot plans in litres, so it needs your tank size.
smart.hw_flows: Flows that turn on More hot water
smart.hw_flows_none: None. Only Autopilot will heat hot water.
smart.hw_flows_found: They'll heat hot water outside Autopilot's plan. Turn them off, or keep them for notifications.
smart.hw_flows_unknown: Couldn't read your Flows. Turn off any that turn on More hot water on a schedule.
smart.hw_free: On a day off, when do you use the most hot water?
smart.hw_household_learns: Autopilot starts from your answers and learns your real use from your heat pump. After about two weeks it relies on what it has learned. You can change these any time.
smart.hw_work: On working days, when do you mostly shower?
smart.hw_busy: Weekdays with more hot water in the evening
smart.household_invalid: Choose the number of people and a shower time.
smart.hw_daytype_calendar: Today: __type__. Saturdays and Sundays are days off. Mark holidays, vacations and days at home as days off on the Main device, or with a Flow that follows your calendar, so they don't shape your working-day plan.
smart.hw_daytype_set: Today: __type__, set on the Main device or by a Flow. Mark holidays, vacations and days at home as days off, so they don't shape your working-day plan.
smart.hw_reserve_hint: The least hot water Autopilot always keeps. More means heating in a more expensive hour now and then.
smart.hw_reserve_invalid: Pick how much hot water to always keep.
smart.solar_intro: Heat your hot water using excess solar production.
smart.solar_scanning: Looking for energy meters in your home…
smart.solar_meter_pick: Several found. Pick the one for your whole home.
smart.solar_evidence: In recent weeks you sent up to __kw__ kW to the grid in sunny hours.
smart.solar_evidence_plain: Your meter sends power to the grid in sunny hours.
smart.solar_live: Heat hot water when you're selling solar
smart.solar_live_hint: Heats hot water while your home exports power.
smart.solar_forecast_hint: Skips heating at night when sun is forecast, and pauses itself if the forecast keeps missing. Leave it off if a battery or car charger uses your solar first.
smart.solar_no_meter_found: Found your solar panels, but no electricity meter that measures what you sell, like a P1 reader. Add it to Homey Energy, then come back here.
smart.solar_need_meter: Solar heating needs an electricity meter that measures what you sell, like a P1 reader. Add it to Homey Energy, then come back here.
smart.hw_reserve_20: 20 L, a rinse or the dishes
smart.mode_note: Live steers your heat pump. Simulated previews the plan without making changes.
smart.indoor_intro: Autopilot keeps it at your thermostat's setting.
smart.indoor_homey_desc: One sensor, or the average of several rooms.
smart.indoor_note: Autopilot steers your heat pump through the outdoor temperature (BT1). Requires room-sensor control on your heat pump to be off.
smart.indoor_source_prompt: More than one sensor reports this. Choose the one for Autopilot.
smart.indoor_bt50_note: The room temperature is still sent to your heat pump as BT50 to prevent sensor alarms.
smart.range_intro: How far the indoor temperature may move while Autopilot heats more in cheap hours and less in expensive ones. You can change this later in Heating setup.
smart.range_example: Example day: cheap night, expensive evening
smart.range_fact_cools: The house cools below your temperature when a peak costs more than
smart.range_feel_comfortable: Autopilot mostly heats more in the cheapest hours. Each degree the house cools has to be bought back later, so it lets the house cool only when a peak costs much more than the hours after it. Most days the temperature stays where you set it.
smart.range_feel_save_some: On a day with an expensive evening, the house is 1–2 °C warmer in the morning and 1–2 °C cooler during the evening peak.
smart.range_feel_save_most: Autopilot uses the whole range whenever prices change. Expect the house to be several degrees warmer before expensive hours and several degrees cooler during them.
smart.custom_warning: For advanced users. These settings apply to the Heating device when its comfort range is Custom. Autopilot is tuned for the three standard ranges. Other values are untested and may heat more, save less or let the house get colder than expected.
smart.custom_coldest_hint: How far the house may cool below its indoor temperature while Autopilot eases off.
smart.custom_warmest_hint: How far a pre-heat may take the house above its indoor temperature.
smart.custom_price_ratio_hint: Heat is moved between two hours only when the expensive one costs at least this many times the cheap one. Lower moves heat more often.
smart.custom_coast_hours_hint: How long the house may run on stored heat before Autopilot heats it back up.
smart.custom_preheat_shift_hint: How far below the measured outdoor temperature Autopilot may send BT1, to heat more.
smart.custom_coast_shift_hint: How far above the measured outdoor temperature Autopilot may send BT1, to heat less.
smart.custom_comfort_weight_hint: What a degree away from your temperature costs against the money a shift saves. Higher keeps the house closer to your temperature.
smart.custom_preheat_lead_label: How early a pre-heat may start
smart.custom_preheat_lead_hint: As a share of how slowly your house warms and cools (its time constant). 1 lets a pre-heat start a full time constant before a price peak.
smart.curve_intro: When Autopilot isn't running, your heat pump goes by its heating curve alone. After a week, Autopilot knows how far off it is.
smart.curve_auto_desc: Autopilot changes the curve offset (menu 1.1.1) once, by up to 3 steps, and tells you in the Timeline. You can undo it here.
smart.curve_self_desc: Autopilot tells you in the Timeline what to change. Look for it after the first week.
smart.curve_advice_row: Change the curve offset from __from__ to __to__ (menu 1.1.1)
smart.hw_plan_link: How Autopilot picks when to heat
smart.hw_plan_s1: Morning showers. Hot water drops below its start temperature
smart.hw_plan_s2: Heats to 60 °C right away. This time in the morning's expensive hours
smart.hw_plan_s3: Late showers. Hot water drops again
smart.hw_plan_s4: Heats to 60 °C right away. This time the price is lower
smart.hw_plan_w1: Heats to 56 °C. The night is the cheapest, and that covers the day
smart.hw_plan_w3: Evening showers. Still from the night's heating
smart.hw_plan_u1: Heats to 48 °C, enough for the morning
smart.hw_plan_u3: The rest at noon to 55 °C, on your own solar power
smart.hw_plan_d1: Heats to 50 °C: just enough for the morning
smart.hw_plan_d3: Prices dip at 14:00, so it tops up there for the evening
smart.hw_plan_b2: A bath nobody planned. Hot water runs low
smart.hw_plan_b3: A new plan: a top-up now, in the cheapest hour left before the evening
smart.hw_legionella_intro: Every __days__ days Autopilot heats the water hot enough to kill legionella, in the cheapest hours. If the water already got that hot, it skips it.
smart.hw_legionella_note: Your heat pump's own periodic hot water is turned off. Turn Autopilot off and it comes back.
smart.exp_settling_sub: Up to 1 °C off for a while
smart.exp_follow: Follow along with the __widget__ widget. Daily updates come in the timeline until it's done.

changes.autopilot_simulated: Autopilot · Simulated. Previews the plan without making changes
changes.autopilot_uses: Used by Autopilot, so they stay on while it runs

gateway.title: Gateway connection
gateway.hint: Choose how your gateway numbers NIBE Modbus address 40025. Not sure? Ask whoever set it up.
gateway.invalid: Choose a gateway, a port from 1–65535 and a Modbus ID from 1–247.
gateway.detect_intro: Checking the values your heat pump reports. This may take a few minutes, depending on the gateway.

firmware.title: Update your heat pump first
firmware.intro: Many features require recent software on your heat pump. Older versions lack some readings and can report wrong energy figures.
firmware.online_body: When an update is available, approve it in the myUplink app or on your heat pump's display. Swipe to the product overview and tap Update.
firmware.usb_body: Download the latest software from myuplink.com and put it on a USB stick. Insert it in the port above the display and open menu 8.1.
firmware.f_title: Via myUplink or a USB stick
firmware.f_body: The steps differ between models. See your heat pump's manual.
firmware.note: This takes a few minutes. Your settings are kept.

backup.title: Save your current settings
backup.intro: Optional. Your heat pump can keep a copy of all its settings on a USB stick, so you can go back to them later, with or without Nibe Live.
backup.insert_body: In the port above the display. Menu 8 appears.
backup.save_body: Open menu 8.3 Manage settings and choose Save settings. Keep the stick.
backup.restore_body: Insert the stick and choose Restore settings in menu 8.3. This replaces every setting, including changes made since, and can't be undone.

hotwater.cal_waiting: Heating cycles recorded so far: __CYCLES__. Two that heat the water differently are needed before the tank size can be worked out.
